Encode and decode text by swapping each letter with its mirror in the alphabet.

<a class="nomi-rough-badge" href="#rough-edges">rough edges</a> Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/atbash-cipher) (MIT). Listed under [Encoding & Ciphers](/examples/?subject=encoding-and-ciphers).

```nomi-run
// FILE: atbash_cipher.nomi
//# The Atbash cipher: each letter swaps with its mirror in the alphabet, `a`
//# with `z`, `b` with `y`, and so on. Digits pass through unchanged, and
//# everything else is dropped.

/// Each lowercase letter and its mirror.
once mirror = Iter.zip('a'..='z', Iter.reverse('a'..='z')) |> Iter.to_map()

/// The ciphertext of `phrase`, in lowercase groups of five.
pub fn encode(phrase: String) -> String {
    phrase
    |> translate()
    |> Iter.chunks(5)
    |> Iter.map(&String.join(&1))
    |> String.join(" ")
}

/// The plaintext of `phrase`, with no spaces.
pub fn decode(phrase: String) -> String {
    phrase |> translate() |> String.join()
}

/// Each letter and digit of `text` in cipher order. The cipher is its own
/// inverse, so this both encodes and decodes.
fn translate(text: String) -> List<String> {
    text
    |> String.to_lower()
    |> String.to_codepoints()
    |> Iter.map(swap)
    |> Maybe.values()
    |> Iter.map(Codepoint.to_string)
    |> Iter.to_list()
}

fn swap(cp: Codepoint) -> Maybe<Codepoint> {
    if Codepoint.digit?(cp) {
        Some(cp)
    } else {
        Map.get(mirror, cp)
    }
}

// FILE: atbash_cipher_test.nomi
import atbash_cipher

test "encode" {
    cases = [
        #("encode yes", "yes", "bvh"),
        #("encode no", "no", "ml"),
        #("encode OMG", "OMG", "lnt"),
        #("encode spaces", "O M G", "lnt"),
        #("encode mindblowingly", "mindblowingly", "nrmwy oldrm tob"),
        #("encode numbers", "Testing,1 2 3, testing.", "gvhgr mt123 gvhgr mt"),
        #("encode deep thought", "Truth is fiction.", "gifgs rhurx grlm"),
        #(
            "encode all the letters",
            "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
            "gsvjf rxpyi ldmul cqfnk hlevi gsvoz abwlt",
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, phrase, expected), description {
        assert atbash_cipher.encode(phrase) == expected
    }
}

test "decode" {
    cases = [
        #("decode exercism", "vcvix rhn", "exercism"),
        #(
            "decode a sentence",
            "zmlyh gzxov rhlug vmzhg vkkrm thglm v",
            "anobstacleisoftenasteppingstone",
        ),
        #("decode numbers", "gvhgr mt123 gvhgr mt", "testing123testing"),
        #(
            "decode all the letters",
            "gsvjf rxpyi ldmul cqfnk hlevi gsvoz abwlt",
            "thequickbrownfoxjumpsoverthelazydog",
        ),
        #("decode with too many spaces", "vc vix    r hn", "exercism"),
        #(
            "decode with no spaces",
            "zmlyhgzxovrhlugvmzhgvkkrmthglmv",
            "anobstacleisoftenasteppingstone",
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, phrase, expected), description {
        assert atbash_cipher.decode(phrase) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The cipher is a map from each letter to its mirror, `Iter.zip('a'..='z', Iter.reverse('a'..='z')) |> Iter.to_map()`, built once. Arithmetic on code point numbers (`219 - n`) was the other option; the map shows the two alphabets the description shows.
- `translate` works on code points, since the cipher is ASCII. `swap` keeps a digit and looks a letter up in the map, so anything else answers `None` and `Maybe.values` drops it.
- The cipher is its own inverse, so `encode` and `decode` share `translate` and differ only in how they join the letters: groups of five from `Iter.chunks(5)`, or one run.
- Each canonical group is a test named by the group's description, holding one `subtests` table; a `group` block is for shared `clock`, `boot` or `setup`, which none needs.

## Rough edges

Where Nomi made this exercise harder than it should be. Each is an open question for the language, not a settled answer.

- **A missing feature.** A function with a defaulted parameter cannot be passed where a function of fewer parameters is expected, so joining each group of five is `Iter.map(&String.join(&1))` rather than `Iter.map(String.join)`. The error's hint names the capture to write:

  ```
  error: argument 2: expected (List<String>) -> U, got (Iter<String>, String) -> String
    = help: defaults do not apply to a function value, so pass a capture that calls it: &String.join(&1)
  ```
